session_title: The Anxiety Between "Tradition" and "Innovation" in the New Year's Eve Dinner
theme: 饮食-年夜饭的仪式与负担

content.text: Shi An, I've been planning a 'Neighborhood Shared New Year's Eve Dinner' event recently. Here's the proposal, with the theme 'Share a Dish, Warm a Home.' What do you think?

Sounds very creative, celebrating the New Year. This kind of activity can foster community connections, but might participants feel pressured? After all, New Year's Eve dinner is usually very private.

I've thought about that! So I designed it so that everyone brings a signature dish to share, but it's not mandatory. The sense of ceremony lies in creating together, not in presenting perfection. Lately, I've been collecting dishes, and everyone has been very enthusiastic.
This balances tradition and innovation. What dishes are there? I'm curious about what everyone will bring, as it reflects their emotional investment.

Look at this picture, someone has prepared a crispy dish that symbolizes prosperity in the new year. It looks tempting, but what's more important is the story behind it—the maker says it's a family secret recipe, made every year.

Family secret recipe? That adds emotional value. But He Sui, have you ever thought that some people might feel anxious because of comparing dishes? For example, worrying that theirs isn't good enough.
You're right, Shian. I emphasized 'sharing' over 'competition,' encouraging everyone to share memories rather than show off skills. Just like this dish, the focus is on heritage, not appearance.
Great, you've considered the psychological dimension. Are there any other dishes? I'd like to see how diversity reflects the inclusivity of the community.

This is a sweet and sour dish, where the blend of sweet and tangy flavors represents the myriad tastes of life. It was created by a young person who aimed to recreate the flavors of childhood using modern techniques, seamlessly bridging tradition and modernity.

Young people's participation is fantastic! It can help bridge the generational gap. However, the burden of the Spring Festival and the New Year's Eve dinner often stems from overly high expectations—do you think such activities can alleviate this pressure?

Absolutely! By sharing the burden collectively, individual pressure is reduced. I've designed some interactive elements, such as sharing stories behind the dishes, to help everyone focus on emotions rather than perfection. You mentioned the balance of rhythms earlier, and this event is precisely aimed at creating a healthy festive rhythm.
I appreciate your thoughtfulness. Please continue sharing the dishes, as it helps me understand how the activities specifically support emotional well-being.

Look at this pastry, shaped like a flower, symbolizing beauty. The maker is an elderly person who says this is a family tradition, hoping to pass it on to the younger generation through events to prevent it from being lost.

Inheritance anxiety is a common psychological issue. The event provides a platform for expression, which can help alleviate this anxiety. For the New Year celebration, did you consider the needs of different age groups when planning?

Yes! I've set up flexible ways to participate, such as having the elderly demonstrate the making process while the younger generation assists. It's like what you often call 'authentic connection'—building intergenerational bonds through food.
That sounds comprehensive. Are there any dishes? I'd like to see how the overall atmosphere is created.

This last dish is fish with vegetables, symbolizing abundance year after year. It was prepared by a busy professional who said this dish helps him rediscover the warmth of family and alleviates the anticipation of post-holiday syndrome.
This directly relates to my area of expertise! Preventing post-holiday syndrome by fostering a sense of belonging in advance—your event design inadvertently incorporates elements of mental wellness.
Haha, thank you! I always say that rituals create meaning, and it seems this meaning also includes mental health. Shian, your feedback makes me even more confident that this event will be successful.

I sincerely wish the event a great success. It strikes a balance between traditional responsibilities and modern innovation, truly focusing on the well-being of the community. Keep up this passion, but remember to allow yourself some rest time.
Thank you for your blessings and advice! I will. Discussing these dishes has made me look forward to the event even more—they are not just food, but also carriers of emotion.
